swpmProcedures.title: MIL-C-26500 Front Release Contact Removal & Crimp Procedure
swpmProcedures.summary: Verified disassembly, front-face contact removal, and M22520 crimping rules for BACC45FM/FS/FN/FT/FP and BACC63AE/AF/BN/BP/BV/CB/CC/CS/DW/DY connectors.
steps: Inspect removal tool tip/bit before use — do not use a removal tool with a bent tip or bit (injury and clip damage hazard).
If backshell removal is required, push backshell components away WITHOUT removing the rear grommet from the connector.
At the FRONT face of the connector, axially align the removal tool (plunger fully retracted) with the contact cavity.
Select verified crimp tool & turret setting from SWPM 20-61-11 Table 48 (M22520/1-01 + M22520/1-02 Red/Blue/Yellow or M22520/2-01 + M22520/2-02) matching wire AWG and contact size.
Seal all empty contact cavities with approved seal plugs/rods per SWPM 20-61-11 Para 3.C.
warnings: DO NOT INSERT THE REMOVAL TOOL INTO THE REAR GROMMET OF THE CONNECTOR. DAMAGE TO THE CONNECTOR WILL OCCUR (SWPM 20-61-11 Para 6.C).
DO NOT USE MORE THAN THE NECESSARY AMOUNT OF FORCE — DAMAGE TO CONTACT RETENTION CLIPS CAN OCCUR.

swpmProcedures.title: Rear Release Contact Removal, Retry Rotation & Grommet Protection
swpmProcedures.summary: Verified rear-face contact extraction procedure for BACC63ED/EE/EF, BACC63CM/CN/CT/CU/DB/DC, MIL-C-83723 Series III, and Deutsch DL rear-release connectors.
steps: Select the verified rear-release removal tool matching contact size and wire O.D. (if wire O.D. is too large for the tool, contact must be replaced per SWPM 20-63 Para 2.B).
At the REAR of the connector, place removal tool on the wire and align axially with the contact cavity near the grommet surface.
Push removal tool smoothly until it stops, then pull wire and removal tool out of the cavity simultaneously without excessive force.
If contact fails to release: FULLY REMOVE the tool from the cavity BEFORE rotating approximately 90 degrees and retrying (max 4 attempts before replacement).
warnings: THE REMOVAL TOOL MUST BE REMOVED FROM THE CONTACT CAVITY WHEN THE TOOL IS TURNED. IF NOT REMOVED, DAMAGE TO RETENTION CLIPS CAN OCCUR (SWPM 20-63 Para 2.A).
Never pull wire and removal tool with excessive force — retention clip or rear grommet damage can occur.

swpmProcedures.category: Conductor Size Adjustment (Small Wire in Larger Barrel)
swpmProcedures.title: Contact Assembly with Folded-Back Conductor, Filler Wire, or Eyelet
swpmProcedures.summary: Verified Boeing SWPM 20-60 procedure when wire conductor AWG is smaller than the contact crimp barrel size.
toolsRequired: Applicable Contact Crimp Tool (Selected for Adjusted Wire Size)
steps: Determine approved adjustment method: Folded-back conductor (Para 2.A), Filler wire(s) (Para 2.B), or Eyelet (Para 2.C).

For folded-back conductor (SWPM 20-60 Table): 26 AWG in Sz 20 barrel -> Adjusted 22 AWG; 24/22 AWG in Sz 16 barrel -> Adjusted 20 AWG; 20 AWG in Sz 12 -> Adjusted 16 AWG; 18 AWG in Sz 12 -> Adjusted 14 AWG.
Find standard insulation removal length for the crimp barrel size and MULTIPLY BY TWO for folded-back preparation.
Strip insulation cleanly without nicking or cutting any conductor strands; fold conductor neatly and crimp using the tool setting for the adjusted wire size.
warnings: DO NOT CUT OR CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE STRANDS OF THE CONDUCTOR. THE MECHANICAL STRENGTH OF THE WIRE CAN BE DECREASED (SWPM 20-60 Para 2.A).

swpmProcedures.title: ARINC 600 Insert Compatibility, Quadrax Removal & Lubricant Rules
swpmProcedures.summary: Verified Boeing SWPM 20-71 rules for BACC66 / ARINC 600 connectors, quadrax contacts (BACC47GA/GB), and empty cavity sealing.
steps: Before removing BACC47GA/GB quadrax contacts, move the seal boot rearward away from the contact cavity and inspect removal tool 1738894-1 for bent/damaged tips.
When installing ARINC 600 inserts, align keyway with shell key and reinstall retainer plates with initial screws and washers.
Seal all empty contact cavities from the rear until seal plug shoulder sits flush against insert surface.
Verify polarization post positions per SWPM 20-71 Table 146 before mating.
warnings: AN INSERT OF AN ARINC 600 CONNECTOR FROM ONE SUPPLIER MUST NOT BE USED IN A CONNECTOR SHELL FROM A DIFFERENT SUPPLIER (SWPM 20-71 Para 19).
DO NOT USE A SILICONE, TEFLON, OR OTHER NON-CONDUCTIVE OR SPRAY LUBRICANT — IT WILL PREVENT SATISFACTORY CONTACT OPERATION.

swpmProcedures.title: Wire Harness Contamination Removal & EWIS Arcing / Chafing Prevention
swpmProcedures.summary: Verified Boeing SWPM 20-00, 20-02, and 20-10 procedures for cleaning external and internal wire harness contamination and preventing arcing/chafing.
toolsRequired: Approved Solvent or Aqueous Cleaner per SWPM 20-10
steps: Eliminate all ignition sources (flames, smoking, spark-producing tools/test equipment) prior to solvent cleaning (SWPM 20-02).
Classify contamination: Heavy solvent-soluble (Para 3.A), Aqueous-soluble (Para 3.B), Solid debris (Para 3.C), or Light fluid/particle contamination (Para 3.D / 4.A).
Apply specific precautions around Environmentally Sealed Connectors (Para 4.B) vs Unsealed Connectors (Para 4.C) to prevent fluid ingress into contact cavities.
Inspect supports, backshells, strain relief clamps, and bundle routing for chafing, fluid residue, or debris before close-out.
warnings: ARCING CAN OCCUR TO THE WIRING DUE TO CONTACT WITH FLUIDS. CHAFING CAN OCCUR TO WIRE INSULATION DUE TO CONTACT WITH DEBRIS (SWPM 20-00).
Tools and test equipment that can make a spark must not be used in hazardous/fuel-vapor areas (SWPM 20-02).

swpmProcedures.title: M22520/1-01 (AF8 / Astro 615708) & M22520/2-01 (AFM8 / Astro 615717) Operation
swpmProcedures.summary: Hangar setup guide for standard 12-26 AWG (M22520/1-01) and miniature 20-32 AWG (M22520/2-01) MIL-DTL-22520 four-indent contact crimp tools, turret color indexing, and bayonet positioner changes.
steps: Verify the required SWPM Chapter 20 selector setting and turret/positioner P/N for the exact contact P/N and wire AWG.

On M22520/1-01 (AF8 / 615708): pull and rotate the depth selector dial to the SWPM selector code; push the turret release latch, rotate to the matching Red/Blue/Yellow index, and press firmly to lock.
On M22520/2-01 (AFM8 / 615717): install the exact M22520/2-XX bayonet positioner with a quarter turn and verify the data placard matches the contact size.

Strip the wire per SWPM strip length, insert the conductor fully into the crimp barrel until visible in the inspection hole, seat the contact in the tool, and close handles through the full ratchet cycle.
Inspect crimp indents, conductor visibility in the inspection hole, and confirm a small clearance gap between insulation and non-insulated contact barrel.
warnings: Never force or back out a partially crimped cycle — complete the full ratchet stroke before releasing.
Verify tool calibration and Go/No-Go gage check before crimping flight-critical or EWIS harness contacts.

swpmProcedures.swpmRef: Tooling Guide — AD-1377 / 3137CT Moistureproof Splice Tool (SWPM 20-30)
swpmProcedures.title: AD-1377 / 3137CT Environmental Moistureproof Splice & Endcap Crimping (D-436 / BACS12H)
swpmProcedures.summary: Procedure and part-number cross-reference for Raychem D-436 environmental moistureproof inline splices, parallel stub splices, and endcaps in wet or unpressurized aircraft zones.
toolsRequired: AD-1377 (Raychem / TE) or Sargent 3137CT Moistureproof Splice Crimp Tool
Approved Heat Gun with Reflector Nozzle
D-436-36/-37/-38 (Tin) or D-436-82/-83/-84 (Nickel) Inline Environmental Splices
D-436-0128/-58/-59 (Tin) or D-436-0119/-75/-76 (Nickel) Parallel / Endcap Splices
steps: Select moistureproof environmental splices (Red 26-20 AWG, Blue 20-16 AWG, Yellow 16-12 AWG) for all wet areas and zones outside the pressure cabin.
Slide the transparent heat-shrink sealing sleeve onto the wire BEFORE stripping and crimping the metal barrel.
Strip conductors per SWPM 20-30, insert into the matching color cavity of the AD-1377 / 3137CT tool, and complete the full crimp cycle on each side of the barrel.
Center the sealing sleeve over the crimped barrel and apply uniform heat until the sealing rings melt and flow cleanly at both ends while keeping the sleeve transparent.
Verify conductor visibility, absence of charring/bubbling, and full 360-degree adhesive seal around the wire insulation.
warnings: EWIS CRITICAL: Never substitute dry-area non-moistureproof splices in pressurized-boundary, wheel well, wing, bilge, or exterior wet zones.
Do not overheat the heat-shrink sleeve — scorching or opaque browning indicates insulation damage and requires rework.

swpmProcedures.title: AMP Certi-Crimp PIDG Terminal Tools (59250 T-Head, 47386-4 Red, 47387-7 Blue, 46121 Yellow)
swpmProcedures.summary: Selection, tightness-setting adjustment, and crimp inspection guide for Pre-Insulated Diamond Grip (PIDG / AS7928) ring/faston terminals and dry-zone splices.
toolsRequired: AMP 59250 Certi-Crimp T-Head (Red 22-18 AWG & Blue 16-14 AWG PIDG Terminals / Parallel Splices)
AMP 47386-4 Red PIDG Terminal & Non-MP Splice Tool (22-16 AWG)
AMP 47387-7 Blue PIDG Terminal & Non-MP Splice Tool (16-14 AWG)
AMP 46121 Yellow PIDG Terminal Tool (26-22 AWG)
steps: Match terminal color and wire AWG to the dedicated AMP tool: Yellow 26-22 AWG (46121), Red 22-16 AWG (47386-4), Blue 16-14 AWG (47387-7), or dual-cavity T-Head 59250 for Red/Blue PIDG terminals.
Seat the PIDG terminal properly in the matching color die cavity so the insulation support sleeve aligns with the rear insulation-grip nest.
Insert the stripped conductor until wire strands just extend slightly past the barrel into the inspection bellmouth; squeeze handles until the Certi-Crimp ratchet releases.
Adjust insulation-grip tightness pins (1 = tightest, 3 or 4 = loosest) if insulation is cut/pierced or slips during pull check.
Verify conductor protrusion, intact colored nylon sleeve, and firm strain-relief grip on wire insulation.
warnings: AMP 59250 T-Head does NOT have clearance for standard non-moistureproof butt splices — use dedicated 47386-4 (Red) or 47387-7 (Blue) instead.
Never crimp uninsulated terminals in PIDG insulated-grip dies.

swpmProcedures.swpmRef: Tooling Guide — Burndy M8ND + N14HT Die & BMS13-55 Fire Wire Stripper (CFM56)
swpmProcedures.title: 737NG CFM56 Fire Detector High-Temp Terminal Crimping (Burndy M8ND-N14HT & BMS13-55)
swpmProcedures.summary: Specialized stripping and crimping workflow for 737NG CFM56 engine hot-section fire detector wire (BMS13-55 Type 2 Class 1 AWG 18) and YAV14G88 high-temperature nickel terminals.
toolsRequired: Dedicated Fire Detector Wire Stripper (Knife-Edge Blades for BMS13-55)
Burndy N14HT Die Set (for YAV14G88 High-Temp Terminal)
steps: Use ONLY the dedicated fire-detector wire stripper on BMS13-55 tough high-temp insulation; standard strippers shred the jacket and damage strands.
Strip the conductor so a small portion of bare conductor remains visible through the inspection opening of the YAV14G88 terminal lug per Boeing SWPM.
Install the N14HT die set into the Burndy M8ND frame and rotate the head to verify the correct cavity marking.
Orient the YAV14G88 terminal so the indent forms on top of the crimp barrel and the rear insulation flanges sit in the rounding nest.
Close the handles completely so the flanges wrap into a smooth round strain-relief clamp around the insulation, then inspect for cracked flanges or loose strands.
warnings: EWIS CRITICAL (Engine Fire Zone): Never use standard wire strippers on BMS13-55 fire detector wire — frayed insulation compromises fire-zone integrity.
Verify exact YAV14G88 terminal P/N and SWPM torque limits before re-attaching engine fire detector lugs.

swpmProcedures.swpmRef: Tooling Guide — M22520/5-01 (DMC HX4 / Astro 620175 / Kings KTH-1000) Coax Tool
swpmProcedures.title: M22520/5-01 (DMC HX4 / Astro 620175 / KTH-1000) Coaxial Connector & K-Grip Crimping
swpmProcedures.summary: Coaxial RF cable preparation and hexagonal K-Grip ferrule crimping reference using M22520/5-01 (HX4) frame and interchangeable MIL-DTL-22520/5 hex die sets per SWPM 20-51.
toolsRequired: M22520/5-01 Coax Crimp Frame (DMC HX4 / Astro 620175 / AK100 / Kings KTH-1000)
Applicable M22520/5-XX Hex Die Set (per SWPM 20-51 connector table)
Coaxial Cable Stripper & Heat Gun (for Environmental Heat-Shrink Boot)
steps: Verify aircraft effectivity, WDM coax cable code, and SWPM 20-51 connector/die cross-reference before cutting cable.
Slide the heat-shrink environmental sleeve and K-Grip ferrule onto the coaxial cable before stripping the outer jacket, braid, and dielectric.
Crimp the center contact per SWPM 20-51, seat the connector body cleanly between the outer braid and dielectric, and slide the K-Grip sleeve flush into place.
Position the K-Grip ferrule squarely inside the M22520/5-XX hexagonal die nest in the HX4 / M22520/5-01 tool and complete the full ratchet stroke.
Confirm both rubber environmental seals seat properly at the hex crimp edges, then shrink the outer sleeve uniformly with a heat gun.
warnings: Never allow stray outer shield braid strands to touch the center conductor — verify zero short and continuity before antenna connection.
Always cross-check equivalent DMC Y-series / M22520/5-XX die codes against the primary Boeing SWPM 20-51 table.

swpmProcedures.swpmRef: Tooling Guide — 500 VDC Megohmmeter & Aircraft Cable Tracer
swpmProcedures.title: Insulation Resistance Testing (Megohmmeter) & Open/Short Wire Fault Tracing
swpmProcedures.summary: Safe hangar procedures for high-voltage insulation resistance testing (Megger at 500 VDC) and non-destructive open/short wire isolation using an active signal aircraft cable tracer.
toolsRequired: Aircraft Cable Tracer (Active Signal Generator + Receiver Probe)
steps: MEGOHMMETER: Pull associated circuit breakers and DISCONNECT ALL computers, LRUs, sensors, and solid-state components attached to the wire under test per AMM/SWPM.
Connect the Megohmmeter leads between the isolated wire and aircraft ground (or adjacent shield/wire), select 500 VDC test mode, and verify Gigaohm-range insulation integrity.

CABLE TRACER (OPEN CIRCUIT): Connect the active transmitter lead to the broken wire, set coarse sensitivity (x1 / x10 / x100) and fine dial, and trace along the harness until signal drops sharply at the break point.

CABLE TRACER (SHORT TO GROUND): Switch to 'Short' mode, connect transmitter between shorted wire and aircraft structure, and follow the closed-loop signal until reception fades past the fault location.
warnings: CRITICAL EQUIPMENT DAMAGE WARNING: 500 VDC from a Megohmmeter will instantly destroy avionics LRUs and logic gates — verify EVERY connected connector is disconnected first!
Verify flammable vapor / fuel tank safety precautions before applying test voltages in fuel or hazardous zones.
